question_vi: Virtual Threads (Java 21) trong Spring Boot 3.2 hoạt động thế nào? Khác gì WebFlux?
question_en: How do Virtual Threads (Java 21) work in Spring Boot 3.2? How do they differ from WebFlux?
answer_vi:
**Virtual Threads** (Project Loom, Java 21) là thread cực nhẹ do JVM quản lý — không phải OS thread. Bật trong Spring Boot 3.2+ bằng **1 dòng config**: `spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true` — Spring Boot tự dùng cho Tomcat, `@Async`, `@Scheduled`.

**Vì sao đáng giá:** OS thread tốn ~1MB stack, context switch nặng → giới hạn vài nghìn. Virtual Thread tốn ~KB, chạy được hàng triệu; khi block I/O (DB call, HTTP) nó **unmount khỏi carrier thread** để carrier phục vụ request khác → code blocking quen thuộc scale như non-blocking.

| | **Virtual Threads** | **WebFlux (Reactive)** |
|---|---|---|
| Code style | Blocking (quen thuộc) | Non-blocking (Mono/Flux) |
| Complexity | Thấp | Cao (learning curve) |
| Dùng khi | I/O-bound, CRUD app | High-throughput streaming, backpressure |
| CPU-bound | Không giúp | Không giúp |

**Lưu ý:**
- **MDC/ThreadLocal** dễ leak → dùng Micrometer Observation API thay raw MDC.
- **`synchronized`** pin Virtual Thread vào OS thread → mất lợi ích; dùng `ReentrantLock` (Java 24 đã gỡ hạn chế pinning này — JEP 491; Java 21 vẫn dính).
- Không cải thiện CPU-bound
answer_en:
**Virtual Threads** (Project Loom, Java 21) are ultra-lightweight threads managed by the JVM — not OS threads. Enable in Spring Boot 3.2+ with **one line of config**: `spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true` — Spring Boot uses them for Tomcat, `@Async`, `@Scheduled`.

**Why it matters:** OS threads cost ~1MB stack with heavy context switches → capped at a few thousand. Virtual Threads cost ~KB, millions can run; when blocking on I/O (DB calls, HTTP) they **unmount from the carrier thread** so it can serve other requests → familiar blocking code scales like non-blocking.

| | **Virtual Threads** | **WebFlux (Reactive)** |
|---|---|---|
| Code style | Blocking (familiar) | Non-blocking (Mono/Flux) |
| Complexity | Low | High (learning curve) |
| Use when | I/O-bound, CRUD apps | High-throughput streaming, backpressure |
| CPU-bound | No benefit | No benefit |

**Note:**
- **MDC/ThreadLocal** leak easily → use the Micrometer Observation API instead of raw MDC.
- **`synchronized`** pins the Virtual Thread to an OS thread → benefit lost; use `ReentrantLock` (Java 24 removed this pinning limitation — JEP 491; Java 21 still has it).
- No improvement for CPU-bound work
